output.methodChoice: Collected 3 of 3 allowed items. X9 (platform audit trail) showed what CR-118 actually changed. X12 (internal audit recalculation of all night staff, plus a test-tenant re-run) tested whether the shortfalls follow that change and whether flagged records, hours or release 7.4 add anything. X5 (overtime dashboard) tested whether the overtime drop can be separated from the rota trial; it cannot. The bank, hours and data rivals were already weakened by E3 and E5 and were then excluded by X12.
output.brief:
Anika, the October shortfalls came from a configuration change, not your data.

On 22 October an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to the night premium rule, logged as a label-only correction. The template also moved the start of the night premium from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform's tamper-proof audit trail shows this; the start was 20:00 in both trial runs. Internal audit found 147 night workers underpaid, each by exactly the premium for hours worked 20:00–22:00 (8 never complained). Hours worked and bank payments were right.

Ardentra's account doesn't hold up: staff with flagged records were no likelier to be underpaid, and Ardentra's own test copy (current release, current data) paid all 158 night workers correctly once the start was set back to 20:00. I'm highly confident.

Next: reject Malcolm's plan (no suspension, no reload, don't concede clause 14.3). Have Ardentra restore 20:00, re-run October to confirm, and pay all 147 off-cycle before 24 November. Keep release 7.4; it carries the November tax update. Require independent testing of post-freeze changes. Don't pause the rota trial yet: the overtime drop fits both the pay problem and the trial equally; recheck cover once pay is corrected.
